questions.prompt: What is the difference between RUN and CMD?

options.text: RUN runs when the container starts; CMD runs at build time
RUN executes at build time and is baked into the image; CMD is the default command run when a container starts
CMD can appear many times and all of them run

questions.explanation: RUN executes during the build and its result becomes an image layer. CMD sets the default command that runs each time a container starts from the image.

questions.prompt: Does the EXPOSE instruction publish a port so your machine can reach the container?

options.text: Yes, EXPOSE opens the port to the host
No, EXPOSE only documents the port; you still publish it at run time with -p

questions.explanation: EXPOSE is documentation/metadata only. To actually reach the container's port from your machine you publish it with -p host:container at run time.

questions.prompt: In `docker build -t mysite:1.0 .`, what does the trailing dot mean?

options.text: It is the build context — the directory sent to the daemon that COPY reads from

questions.explanation: The dot is the build context: the directory Docker packages and sends to the daemon. COPY can only copy files inside this context.

questions.prompt: The file that lists paths to exclude from the build context is called ______. (filename)
questions.explanation: A .dockerignore file keeps files like .git, node_modules, and .env out of the build context, making builds faster and images cleaner.

questions.prompt: Why is the exec form CMD ["node", "server.js"] preferred over the shell form CMD node server.js?

options.text: It runs the program directly so it receives signals like SIGTERM, allowing docker stop to shut it down cleanly
The shell form is not valid Dockerfile syntax
The exec form runs faster at build time

questions.explanation: The exec (JSON-array) form runs the process directly, so it receives Unix signals. The shell form wraps the command in /bin/sh -c, which can swallow SIGTERM and slow down graceful stops.

questions.prompt: Order these Dockerfile instructions as they should typically appear for a simple app.
questions.explanation: Start from a base image, set the working directory, copy your files in, then declare the default command to run at container start.
